statement: A derived instance is generated with a data or newtype declaration, its body derived syntactically from the type's definition
how: a deriving clause compiles and the instance is usable with no instance declaration

statement: Derived instances are possible only for classes known to the compiler: those defined in the Prelude or a standard library
how: `class C a; data T = A deriving C` is refused

statement: Condition 1: Eq is derivable
how: `data T = A deriving Eq` compiles

statement: Condition 1: Ord is derivable
how: `data T = A deriving (Eq, Ord)` compiles

statement: Condition 1: Enum is derivable
how: `data T = A | B deriving Enum` compiles

statement: Condition 1: Bounded is derivable
how: `data T = A | B deriving Bounded` compiles

statement: Condition 1: Show is derivable
how: `data T = A deriving Show` compiles

statement: Condition 1: Read is derivable
how: `data T = A deriving Read` compiles

statement: Condition 1: a Prelude class outside the six is not derivable
how: `data T = A deriving Num` is refused

statement: Condition 1: Functor is not derivable
how: `data T a = A a deriving Functor` is refused in Haskell 98

statement: Condition 1: Monad is not derivable
how: `data T a = A a deriving Monad` is refused

statement: Condition 2: there must be a context cx' with cx' => C tij for every constituent type tij
how: `data T = T (Int -> Int) deriving Eq` is refused

statement: Condition 2 holds for a user type only if that type is an instance
how: `data U = U; data T = T U deriving Show` is refused

statement: Condition 2 may rest on the derived instance of a type being declared in the same group
how: two mutually recursive types deriving Eq compile

statement: Condition 3: Bounded on an enumeration
how: `data T = A | B | C deriving Bounded` compiles

statement: Condition 3: Bounded on a single constructor with fields
how: `data T = T Bool Char deriving Bounded` compiles

statement: Condition 3: Bounded on neither an enumeration nor a single constructor
how: `data T = A Int | B deriving Bounded` is refused

statement: Condition 4: Enum requires an enumeration
how: `data T = A Int deriving Enum` is refused

statement: Condition 4: one constructor with a field disqualifies the type
how: `data T = A | B Int deriving Enum` is refused

statement: Condition 5: no explicit instance elsewhere in the program may make T an instance of C
how: `data T = A deriving Eq; instance Eq T` is refused

statement: Condition 5 reads "elsewhere in the program": an explicit instance in another module also conflicts
how: a second module with `instance Eq T` for the derived T is refused; whole-program check, see readings.md

statement: For derived instances a newtype is treated as a data declaration with a single constructor
